gaps.sentence: The audience found the lecture extremely ___ (BORE).
gaps.explanation: The lecture causes boredom, so it is boring; the audience would be bored.

gaps.sentence: Her kindness and ___ (GENEROUS) made her very popular.
gaps.explanation: Parallel to 'kindness', a noun is needed: generosity (note the irregular -osity spelling).

gaps.sentence: The editor-in-chief oversees every ___ (EDIT) of the magazine.
gaps.explanation: "Every edition" = every published issue; "editor" is the person.

gaps.sentence: It is ___ to book tickets in advance during the festival (ADVICE).
gaps.explanation: The suffix -able forms the adjective: advisable means worth recommending. 'It is + adjective + to-infinitive'.
After 'in' a noun is needed: excitement (-ment noun).

gaps.sentence: Air ___ (POLLUTE) is a serious problem in big cities.
gaps.explanation: The subject must be a noun: pollution (-tion noun); a pollutant is a specific polluting substance.

gaps.sentence: The crisis could ___ the economic situation (WORSE).
gaps.explanation: The suffix -en forms the verb: worsen means to make worse. A base verb follows 'could'.
After 'an important' a noun is needed: discovery (note the change from -er to -y).
